The evidence suggests a potential dependency on the metabolic or signaling pathways involving 3-Methyl-2(5H)-furanone, which could be a key intermediate in the interaction between the compound and M19-MEL. The integration of these relationships highlights a possible role for 1,5-Di-O-Cis-P-Coumaroylquinic Acid in the regulation of a downstream target, M19-MEL, through a chain of targets that includes LoVo and 3-Methyl-2(5H)-furanone.
